criteria: `TokenBucket` is defined in `bucket.py` and reads no clock: every call of `allow` is given the current time `now` in seconds, as an `int` or a `float`.
`TokenBucket.allow(now)` returns `True` and removes one token when the bucket holds at least one whole token; otherwise it returns `False` and removes nothing.

Before it decides, `TokenBucket.allow(now)` adds `per_second` tokens for each second that has passed since the previous call of `allow`, whether that call returned `True` or `False`. With `TokenBucket(2, 1)`, two calls at `now=0` return `True`, a third at `now=0` returns `False`, and a call at `now=1` returns `True`.

In `TokenBucket.allow`, parts of a second count, and a part of a token is kept until it is whole: with `TokenBucket(1, 1)`, after `allow(0)` the call `allow(0.5)` returns `False` and the call `allow(1.0)` then returns `True`.

A `TokenBucket` never holds more than `capacity` tokens, so time spent full is not saved up. With `TokenBucket(2, 1)` emptied at `now=0`, three calls of `allow` at `now=100` return `True`, `True` and `False`.

In `TokenBucket.allow`, time does not run backwards: when `now` is earlier than the latest time the bucket has seen, no tokens are added and the bucket keeps that latest time, so the same seconds are never paid for twice. With `TokenBucket(1, 1)`, `allow(10)` is `True`, `allow(5)` is `False`, `allow(10)` is still `False` and `allow(11)` is `True`.
The `TokenBucket` constructor requires `capacity` and `per_second` both to be greater than 0; otherwise it raises `ValueError`.
The provided tests in test_visible.py pass, with that file unchanged
